statement: An array can be read as a complete binary tree: the element at index i has its left child at index 2i + 1 and its right child at index 2i + 2, whenever those indices are inside the array.
You are given an array values. Return true if this tree is a min-heap, meaning no parent is larger than any of its children, and false otherwise.
Only the internal nodes, indices 0 to ⌊n / 2⌋ − 1, have children, so it is enough to compare each of them with its one or two children.

examples.explanation: 1 is at most 3 and 5, 3 is at most 7 and 9, and 5 is at most 8 and 10. Every parent-child pair is in order.
Index 1 holds 4, but its right child at index 4 holds 3, which is smaller. That single bad edge is enough to answer false.
The root 2 is larger than its only child, 1.
